what: What real ffmpeg said about the inputs in tests/reference/tts/, frozen so that static/tts/level.js can be checked against something other than itself.
ffmpeg: ffmpeg version 9.0.1 Copyright (c) 2000-2026 the FFmpeg developers
invalidated_by: any change to the filter chain in tts.py - the numbers under tts_py are what that chain produced, not what it ought to
any change to the fixtures under tests/reference/tts/, which is why their sha256 is here
a different ffmpeg, if it moves the numbers: rerun and compare before accepting, because a shifted reference is indistinguishable from a broken level.js unless somebody looks
not_invalidated_by: changes to static/tts/level.js - that is the thing being checked, and regenerating these numbers to make it pass is the one move this file exists to prevent

tones.name: 1000 Hz at 0.1
tones.why: the anchor: K weighting is flat here, so this checks the gating

tones.name: 1000 Hz at 0.5
tones.why: the same tone 14 dB louder - level, not just shape

tones.name: 440 Hz at 0.2
tones.why: K weighting is deliberately not flat here; mitreden froze it too

tones.name: 60 Hz at 0.5
tones.why: down the high pass skirt - the stage nothing else here touches

tones.name: 10000 Hz at 0.2
tones.why: up on the head shelf - a chain without it reads this low

peaks.name: 4000 Hz at 0.5, sampled off the peaks
4000 Hz at 0.25, sampled off the peaks

resampling.name: 1000 Hz survives the way down
resampling.why: well under the new Nyquist rate, so the level must not move

resampling.name: 10000 Hz cannot survive it
resampling.why: above the new Nyquist rate; a resampler without a low pass folds it back to 6050 Hz instead of removing it

utterances.name: quiet
utterances.why: thirty decibels of gain and nothing in the way of it

utterances.name: loud
utterances.why: the gain the other way round, so a sign error cannot hide

utterances.name: short
utterances.why: shorter than the 400 ms block BS.1770 wants, which is the path with no standard behind it - 'Ja!' trimmed hard

utterances.name: burst
utterances.why: a consonant loud enough that reaching the target would breach the ceiling: the gain has to give way, and this is the only case where truePeakDb decides the answer

utterances.name: spike
utterances.why: one sample at full scale - a click, not a sound. Properties only; ffmpeg and level.js do not agree here

disagreements.what: ffmpeg reads these true peaks high. The waveform is a sine, so the real peak is exactly its amplitude - analytic_peak_dbtp - and ffmpeg's 4x interpolator overshoots it. level.js lands on the analytic value. Both are far above sample_peak_dbfs, which is the thing that actually matters.

one sample at full scale drives ffmpeg's loudnorm into its dynamic mode and it hands back a file 3.3 LU quieter than level.js does. Neither answer is audible and neither is wrong; a click is not a sound. Left out of the comparison on purpose rather than left out silently.
